label: first copy step (recall_idx 1) of short sequences (L=3/4) whose remaining outputs are z/o/t/3/j/2/k
explanation: Fires only at step L+1, the step right after <DEL>, where the input is orig(0) fed back and the output is orig(1) (recall_idx == 1). Essentially only for short sequences: L=3 holds 66% of activation mass (7% firing rate there), L=4 holds 34%, L=5 is negligible, and L>=6 never fires. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases or at any later copy step. Within this slot, whether it fires and how strongly depends on which tokens are still left to output (orig(1..L-1)) belonging to a preferred set {z, o, 3, t, 2, j, k} (also weakly e, w). For L=3, at least one of the two remaining outputs must be in the set; for L=4, at least two of three. The strongest activations are L=3 sequences like "k z o <DEL> k" or "i z 3 <DEL> i", where both remaining outputs are in the set and z comes next. The input token (orig(0)) has only weak influence (i, b, j, s are slightly favoured; repeated or digit first tokens slightly less). It is mostly coherent but graded: the token set is soft, which limits precision (~0.55) and recall (~0.75). Mass recall is ~0.88.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: 3, z, o, 2, t, j; least: a, s, d, y) and the second original token (most: z, o, t, 3, j, 2; least: f, 0, y, d); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, recall_idx=1, L=4 & t=5.
